blocks.value: In Lesson 13 you built objects and then filled them in field by field, hoping you did not forget one. A half-initialized object is a bug waiting to happen.

Constructors close that hole: they make it impossible to create an object without supplying what it needs. And **overloading** lets one class offer several ways to be created, so callers can give as much or as little as they have.
What you will be able to do
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

items: Write constructors to create and initialize objects
Explain what a method signature is
Distinguish static members from instance members
